topics.title: Apply in advance
topics.summary: Eligible applicants should apply online at least 4 days before arrival, and medical categories use a 120-day arrival window.
topics.content: The official e-Visa guidance says eligible applicants should apply a minimum of 4 days before the date of arrival. e-Medical and e-Medical Attendant applicants can select an arrival date within a 120-day window.

topics.title: Passport validity and blank pages
topics.summary: Passports should have at least six months validity and at least two blank pages.
topics.content: The official FAQ says the passport should have at least six months validity at the time of application and at least two blank pages for stamping by the Immigration Officer.

topics.title: Required uploads and document language
topics.summary: Applicants must upload a recent photograph and the passport bio page, and supporting documents should be in English.
topics.content: The official portal requires a recent front-facing photograph with a light or white background and the passport bio page containing personal details. It also says supporting documents such as business cards or invitation letters should be in English.

topics.title: Digital photo specifications
topics.summary: Photo uploads should be JPEG, 10 KB to 1 MB, square, front-facing, and on a plain light or white background.
topics.content: The official portal says the digital photo should be JPEG, between 10 KB and 1 MB, equal height and width, front-facing, eyes open, without spectacles, and against a plain light-colored or white background with no shadows or borders.

topics.title: Passport bio page file guidance
topics.summary: The passport bio page is required, and the official site commonly lists PDF uploads up to 300 KB for that document.
topics.content: The official guidance lists the passport bio page as a mandatory upload and commonly shows PDF support from 10 KB to 300 KB for the scanned bio page.

topics.title: ETA and travel passport guidance
topics.summary: Applicants should carry a copy of the ETA and travel with the same passport used for the application.
topics.content: The official portal tells applicants to carry a copy of the Electronic Travel Authorization and confirm ETA status before travel. It also says travelers should use the same passport that was used for the e-Visa application.

topics.title: MVP categories versus official categories
topics.summary: This MVP exposes a smaller category list than the official portal so the hackathon demo stays focused.
topics.content: The production Indian e-Visa portal supports a wider category set. This MVP intentionally narrows that list to a few demo-friendly categories and uses them as simplified prototypes rather than real fee or eligibility advice.

topics.title: Payment is hidden in the MVP flow
topics.summary: Payment is intentionally hidden for now, even though the final SRS includes it later.
topics.content: This implementation keeps the payment experience out of the visible applicant flow for now. The review step remains available, but the payment panel stays hidden until the payments module is turned on later.
